subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for active memory plugins, and what local-file trust boundary should govern files sent to third-party plugin code?
rationale: The request crosses public plugin SDK compatibility and local-file exposure policy, so automation cannot choose the permanent API or security boundary safely.

options.title: Design a narrow SDK seam first
options.body: Define the supported event contract, path authorization, chunk ownership, retry behavior, and compatibility tests before implementing the host delivery path.

options.title: Keep file indexing plugin-owned
options.body: Leave external memory plugins responsible for their own scanning and document the existing helper APIs as the supported low-level reuse surface.

options.title: Defer behind a broader memory backend API
options.body: Track this as part of a larger pluggable memory backend design if maintainers want one unified replacement contract rather than incremental file-event hooks.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow SDK seam first
recommendation.body: Define the supported event contract, path authorization, chunk ownership, retry behavior, and compatibility tests before implementing the host delivery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history around the memory slot and memory host SDK points to steipete as the strongest routing owner for this product/API choice.
